Taama: "Let me tell you about Taama. He has a largest heart of nearly any man and....WHAT? He's coming around later for a drink?…..Shit, have you got any idea what that means? Alright, don't panic. Here's what we'll do. We'll barricade ourselves inside the front living room, load all our weapons just in case, and try and placate the mad fucker with those steaks in the fridge. After he munches on a couple of those, if we're lucky, he'll just leave and go to the pub. Jesus, last time he was here he tore a hole in the back fence and tried to shag Mrs. Johnson's daughter and I'm not going through that hell again…"
Tadgh: Some people you just like. Even if Tadgh was caught shagging his girlfriend on her mother's couch, one rainy night, by both her parents, somehow their adoration of him would be maintained. Generous smile. Cheeky bastard.
Taggart: Taggart became an associate at his law firm a week ago, and he was one of the quickest to do so. Aside from the 60+ hours he puts in every week, after work he's parties like a Roman Emperor. How does he do it? Sure, we know he's smart and he's got attitude, but honestly, does he sleep? I suppose Taggart's defining qualities are that (A) he does what he says he's going to do, (B) he loves the macho chest-thumping male competitive life and (C) he’s very aware that he won't be young and vital forever. Taggart.
Taibe: Taibe isn't the most excitable person in the Kingdom. Hang on, hang on, he's walking but why does he look like he's asleep? Taibe, you awake brother?
Tait: Like an introduced species that is actually fun to have around, Tait is an independent cat who does his own thing, and who tends not to destroy either the environment or his fellow animals. Given that he's a carnivore, biologists aren't certain as to how he does this. He might be predominantly nocturnal, which brings with it its own set of problems. Perhaps we need to put a radio tracker on him?
Taite: Taite is cool and not the arrogant twat many people perceive him to be. He's actually got a wicked sense of humour, although it took him a while to grow into it. After all, so long as you're not hurting anyone, who cares what anyone thinks of you? Sure, he's a little lazy and he takes ages to hand his assignments in, but he gets them in eventually, which his professors appreciate. And yep, he'll get his degree, at which point he might just as easily disappear into Europe for three years with a backpack strapped to him and disregard his earlier career path completely.
Taj: Silky smooth, laid-back and determined, Taj is nowhere near as soft as he sounds. Indeed, he is an incredibly friendly and intuitive soul who has the world at his feet.
Talen: The closest thing he’d ever get to a uniform is the soccer jersey for his local club. Talen is a fine and committed (life) player, although he does need a bit of direction. He’d probably make a good soldier, but we suggest he goes out into the world and finds that direction on his own, not via the orders of someone else who is just taking their own orders.
Tallon: Tallon needs a decent hug. Far more sensitive than he lets on.
Talm: Talm is quite combative when he wants to be. Still waters run deeper than you think here and while he's never the loudest of his group, his opinions are respected by those who know him. What does he do for a living? We have no idea but he's not a bean counter.
Talmage: He's a bizarre cat, alright. Most of the time you won't see him, however, because he'll be digging for old artifacts in Greece, or somewhere.
Talon: Up to his eyeballs in debt.
Tama: Public speaking isn’t really his thing and he doesn't mind a bit of hard work, once he gets his head around it and gets moving, that is. He's strong and he's loyal, and amen to that brother.
Tamlan: Tamlan likes the idea of strapping on a backpack and disappearing into the wilds of the country side with only a leatherman and a sense of adventure, but if push came to shove, via some cataclysmic event and he actually had to do it, he might struggle. He is a deep thinker however, and rarely does he sit down and say to himself, "You know what, right now I'm content with just about every facet of my life." Keep lookin' lad, keep lookin'.....
Tangi: Tangi from the Cook Islands. You want, he get.
Tangles: His reflexes move like a train that has sat on the same piece of line for 30 years and is therefore rusted into place, but he’s an optimistic, funny bloke who can lift a shitload of weight, which has to come in handy sometimes, right?
Tanis:
Raiders of the Lost Ark has a lot to answer for, doesn't it? The city of Tanis, in the movie, is the supposed home of the Ark of the Covenant, which I'm sure is what the parents of Tanis intended him to be. That is, a mystery of god-like proportions that only the very lucky and/or brave will get to behold.
Blah blah blah.....Tanis is a dedicated young man who tends to move with a metal plate stuck to his forehead, which he placed there only to protect his own brain. He tends to run into things head-first, you see, but he’s not a fool. He learned that he had to protect himself. Anyway, that’s Tanis, and this is the life.
Tao: Now, is that fair? Giving a young man a name that is supposed to turn him into a philosophical juggernaut and worldly sage, in general? But he got over his shyness. He got used to being asked about his name. But he does like spending time on his own, on projects and ideas where he can avoid all those pointless questions and comments from others.
Tarant:
It's not that Tarant is lazy, it's just that he detests all the rigmarole involved with any kind of administration. Sure, many of us can say the same thing, but Tarant will dodge, balk and weave, either literally or metaphorically, so he avoids or delays as much pointless red-tape moments as possible. Does this hold him back sometimes? Well, maybe, but he benefits in other ways by having more free time than most. Which begs the question, what are you doing with your spare time, lad? Are you being good for the world or are you just swanning around in an attempt to stay beneath the radar? (Sometimes the path of least resistance is the longest way round.)

Amen.
Taren: A young man brain-washed by images of 6-packed buffoons and absurd hairdos which cover most of your face, Taren needs to toss away his phone and go outside to look at the sky for a while.
Tarks: "Oh, shit yeah!" he replies, after being asked if he wants to come pig shooting, tonight.
Tarkyn: The stealthy crocodile who is either not very bright or just extremely difficult to dissuade from a pre-existing mind-set.
Tarquin: Tarquin is one of those men who, seemingly miraculously, is always, always in tip top form. He is at home inside any social group, his observations are both brilliant and well-timed and he delights in being silly and helping others do the same. There simply isn’t much more to say about the man. Bloody bravo Tarquin.
Taryn: Rarely a liability, Taryn is open minded and clever.
Tase: He's no slacker, but he’s on life number one, according to the reincarnationists, and so his sense of humour, his capacity to be silly and his calm sense of wisdom might take a little longer to evolve.
Tasman: Ocean kayaker. It's a passtime that provides him with the right blend of sustained physical work, pleasure, fresh air and fresh fish, as well as the odd spot of danger.
Tate: Tate loves reconstruction. He might be an air/car crash investigator, a cold case detective or some kind of archeologist. Detail - that's what he's into. And when he gets his teeth into something he's as tenacious as a kelpie.
Tavis: If you're a lady and you're looking for a fellow who is good with his hands, and who loves a bit of handy work around the house, say, mending the eaves, replacing those old hinges on the bathroom door, or perhaps renovating a bedroom, then Tavis is not your man. The last time he tried to hammer a nail into the wall for that calender he bought (sports cars) he broke his thumb and tore out a huge chunk of plaster which he had to pay to get fixed, and hasn't been game to go near any kind of tool since.
Tay: As a ghost that lacks an actual physical body, per se, he gets extremely frustrated, not to mention very thirsty, whenever he attempts to pick up a glass of water because he can’t actually grab the thing. (We hate to say this Tate, but get a job and do it well for 3 months. The stability will do you good.)
Taylor: He recovered quickly after his sex change operation and now headlines at one of Sydney’s most popular cabaret clubs; big smile, great legs.
Tayne: Tayne doesn’t really grasp subtle jokes or hidden meanings. If you need to tell him something, don’t paint it up with a flowery metaphor or some kind of smart analogy thinking he’ll get it. He won’t. Just tell him. Likewise, his answers are brief and the only time you’ll hear him speak for long periods is if he has to read a long document, aloud.
Taz: The reliable and good-natured show pony.
Teale: He’s not a duck! He’s a snake – a great big lazy rainforest python. He drapes himself over limbs all day and likes to chill-out in the shade. He’s a cool customer by default and he rarely looks flustered.
Ted: Ted was a Spitfire pilot in World War 2 and as a very old man with a glint in his eye, he now runs the newsagent on the corner. He’s a lovely old man but he was a tyke in his younger day.
Teddy: An older guy who is all fun-and-games until the shit hits the fan, at which point he tends to fall apart
Telford: Supremely organised, Telford keeps an up-to-date log book for his car and in a perfect world he'd like to have one for his pushbike too. Regimes of order and diligence: this is what Telford enjoys. Note that if he gets called 'Tele' then forget it, he's all over the place with too many friends and too much artistic fun to worry about any kind of order in his life, but not Telford. He wears a suit to work, is part of a strict hierarchy and doesn't mind poverty in the world, so long as he never sees it.
Tem: Tem doesn't just show up, although you might presume that by just looking at him. He asks questions when the time is right, he smiles at strangers, encouraging optimism where possible and he is inquisitive in the world. Does he slip under the radar a bit? Well, I suppose he does. He's certainly never so stressed that he can't sleep at night, and by and large his calming nature is appreciated by all and sundry. Nice work Tem.
Tenpa: His middle Asian origins are 1000’s of years old and it helps him to spread the word of peace. (An aggressive temper is something he never has.)
Teo: A light weight American name, and the title of any individual who gets frightened when someone leaves a door open at the other end of the house, thus allowing a chilly breeze to infiltrate the building.
Terrence: Terrence secretly detests being called Terry, which some people do just to get a rise out of him. He likes fine wine and expensive restaurants, and he went grey very prematurely.
Terry: Okay, sure, once upon a time Terry rhymed with Unreliable and, sometimes, Downright Wrong, but his youthful exuberance came through with the goods. Who wants to grow up anyway? Isn't the world serious enough as it is? People like Terry are here to remind us these things, just don't get him too drunk at the Christmas Party - and if you do, film him. You'll be able to use the defamation evidence in court and it'll probably be funny.
Tex: By any definition Tex is the name of a rocket launch pad, and we know what that means.
Thaddeus:
And already I find myself with a stringent voice, speaking aloud, chest inflated, as if preparing an oration for the high council. 
"Oh Lord Titus, my name is Thaddeus, and I appear before you as a devilish and subversive rogue....."
In reality, of course, he throws tantrums and has the capacity to drive us all quite bonkers.
Thane: The method actor. Loves the stage. Loves Hamlet.
Tharase: The local chief. If you want a decent guide to get you over those mountains and to the sea, beyond, then he's your man.
TheMouse: Big head. Big ears. (With sweet fuck all between them.)
Theo: Theo, I know you’re a good guy. I know you do heaps around the house and I know you’ve got a good heart, but you can’t live with your mother until you’re 40. One day you’ve got to get out there and do it on your own, brother.
Theodor: A staunch royalist. Whether he's English or not, if there is some major royal event happening on television - it might be a wedding, or an anniversary of sorts - Theodor will pull out his royal outfit, which makes him look like a silly kind of sailor, and sit in front of the television drinking cups of tea while grasping a small Union Jack flag. It's quite bizarre.
Theodore: Perhaps not as zealous as his twin brother (Theodor), Theodore still manages to follow some ornate hobby with an obsessive level of intent. And yes, he loves dressing up to express his love of whatever it is he’s into. If he was into World War 2 army paraphernalia, for example, he would delight in dressing up like a humble corporal in the artillery regiment despite having never joined any military service. Likewise if he was nuts about his model train collection, he’d dress up like an old fashioned train driver. I think you get the picture.
Thiago: Thiago walks like he's dancing, which means he's never unhappy, and his Brazilian heritage helps. Remember however that just because he's a dancing Brazilian man doesn't mean he doesn't think deeply or has noble ambitions. Last I heard he was studying corporate finance, or maybe it was environmental law? If it's the latter and he lives in Brazil, then they could really use his help.
Thomas: Earnest and organised if he has no nickname, Thomas has a personality similar to that of a set of architect’s drawings for any modern office block.
Thommo: Thommo is tall, friendly and industrious and just ever so slightly reserved.
Thompson: Thompson was born about 70 years too late. Sadly, the days of chivalrous young men dressed in suits and wearing hats, smoking cigarettes and wooing ladies at dances as a trendy and fashionable thing to do are long past. It's a pity, eh? In a past life Thompson worked for RAF during WW2, in England, intelligence gathering. A refined man these days, he is still highly intelligent, he is awkward around fast women and he likes tinkering on his old Triumph sports car. Unfortunately, the bulk of what constitutes the modern life leaves him quite bored.
Tie: Ironically, Tie is the last person to be tied down to a job, a woman or any kind of long-term obligation. Indeed, he is one free man.
Tiger: A Tasmanian Devil, a North American wildcat or a British bulldog.
Tighe: Too little to box and too large to be a jockey, Tighe might make an excellent gymist. He has energy to burn and he's quick on his feet and some encouragement, here, never goes astray. He's not the scholarly type.
Tim: Tim can be a sneaky little bastard or a genuine legend and, irrespective of which, he is highly intelligent and slides around all decisions quickly. By and large he has very good hand-eye coordination and you can be rest assured that once in his life, and only once, will he say to a fool who is pestering him, “You’re a mere apparition of humanity.”
Timo:
(Pronounced Timmo) As Tim’s  more effervescent alter ego, Timo’ spends more time in the light, and has a greater propensity for absurd, unselfconscious fun. He’ll never run the country and that’s a shame because our world would be happier and far more playful if he did. 
Bravo, Timo’.
Timothy: Timothy is an interesting chap. He's quick and he's clean, and he often stands in front of the mirror of a morning, pulls up his Y-front underpants very high around his waist and says, "Morning Timothy!" He has no problem standing naked in public.
Tino:
No, he's not tiny and he's not tight with money either...well...unless you're outside the family or are a buffoon, which is fair enough. What Tino is, is organised, and he doesn't like surprises, even though he actually operates quite well under pressure. 
Ever seen the TV show M.A.S.H? Well had they found a taller bloke than Radar to play Radar, but who rarely got flustered and who was far more adept with the opposite sex then Tino would be your man. 
 
Note: Tino's mother sends him a hamper every week. It's just how it is.
Tiran: On prima facie evidence there’s no way Tiran could have done it. He’s a dill, sure, but he’s not remotely evil.
Tito: No matter where he's from, Tito loves the USA because it's the only 'civilised' country on earth where you can walk off the street and buy a gun. (Note from Management: Tito, take it back and don't be a fucking idiot.)
TJ: If you want to find T.J on any Saturday afternoon, you need look no further than the betting ring at the local horse races where he can be seen staring up at the latest odds, frowning hard at how he's going to approach the next race.
Tobias: Tobias is not a spectator. He participates because he’s curious and because he wants to help propagate love, peace and humour in the world. True story. Hang shit on him if you want to, but react not when he looks at you like you’re an idiot. For him to do so means you are.
Tobin: Kiwi’s aren’t normal and it’s for this reason that the world barely tolerates them but Tobin is different. Is he the most normal, sane and well-rounded of them all?
Toby: A puny lizard that drops its tail at the first sign of danger, before scurrying back into the undergrowth leaving a trail of blood, fear and goo. (Ironically, perhaps, the only really potent Tobys are completely gay.)
Toci: You’ll never see him in an office and you may not see him standing in the one spot for too long, either. Boats, deserts, exotic women....these are the kinds of things that Toci finds fascinating.
Todd: Todd rhymes with Oops. Not in a catastrophic way, mind you, more in the, I-forgot-to-feed-the-cat-but-now-that-I’ve-remembered-I-will, kind of way.
Tom: While rarely a genius, Tom is a truly good person who is ideal in his role as a big protective brother. (Unless he is unusually small in stature, in which case it’s a different story, and one that tells of speed and ambition.)
Tomas: Head waiter at a five star silver service restaurant. Long fingers and good nails.
Tommy: Haunted by the demons of self-doubt, Tommy throws himself into life in an attempt to combat them, head on. He sports more bruises on his body than anyone and large, complex business issue are difficult for him to get his head around.
Tono: Tono has seen all the Twilight movies three times and he desperately wants to be able to turn himself into a giant werewolf whenever he wants so he can meet girls like whats-her-name. (He's got her poster on his bedroom wall.)
Tony: It’s often difficult to know what’s going on behind the eyes. He could be a great bloke who is honest and friendly and thoughtful, then again he might be a tall sleazy strip of pelican shit. The more outgoing Tony is, however, the more he tends towards the latter. See how you go...
Tor: Tor keeps it simple ‘cause he can. His name evokes images of Scandinavian fjords, smooth running Harley Davidsons and boyish charms, and this is no mean feat.
Torben: It's hard to utter Torben's name with a giant smile on your face and so there a certain sense of gravitas conveyed to the man. Is he serious in adulthood? Well, he certainly has that potential, but the trade off is a staunch work ethic. If Torben ever goes off the rails he probably doesn't do it mildly, although the constrictive nature of his name will largely avoid this. Educated, of strong opinion and well-groomed are some of the things people remember about young Torben but make no mistake, Torben has high moral standards and he is kind. Don't forget that.
Toristen: Toristen puts forward a coherent argument every time. As a barrister with some style he is garnishing a reputation around town. Sure, he's full of it and loves the sound of his own voice, but this kind of ego comes with the territory.
Torquil: We understand that he is from Earth but not much more than that. What we do know is that he is hilariously funny, even if he’s doing something as banal as boiling himself an egg, although no one is sure where he is going or how he intends to get there. At some point we expect he will cease living and this will be a sad day...
Torren:
In the same lineage as Trent and the late James Coburn, Torren is a man whose natural ease and charisma opens most doors quite magically. 
Does he work hard? We have no idea but we doubt it. 
Do the ladies adore him? Yes they do, and if Torren is a gay man then the men adore him even more.
Is he an outdoor, water-kind-of-guy?
If he’s not he should be. 
And his mum loves him more than the rest of her children. (It’s just how it is.) 
The End.
Torrin: Torrin is a doer and a thinker. Rarely incapacitated, Torrin often holds back his more extreme emotions for those times when the crowd is somewhere else.
Tory: It's not that Tory sticks to a tight schedule, on the surface he's not that organised, but his light footedness and his propensity to not sit still for very long means he gets quite a bit done without even meaning to. Basically, if he's being slack you hardly notice, which in turn means he can be quite slack for most of the time. It helps that he has an infectious grin. Generally the girls love him.
Tosawi: Nimble on his feet and dextrous with his hands, Tosawi is deeper than his affable smile lets on. Then again, maybe that's his little secret. He has the capacity to keep things very simple. All he does, in order to achieve this, is act with a good heart at all times. Yeah, it can't always be like this, I mean, shit, he's not a priest or anything, but his path in life is clear cut and uncluttered. Honesty of words and actions will get you a long way. Indeed, it'll get you ALL the way. Tosawi.
Toto: A little one-dimensional, but it’s not his fault. Until they meet him people don’t believe Toto actually exists. The result is a warm, affable man who'd take a bullet for just about anyone. He’s not a corporate heavy weight.
Tovah: The Storm Chaser - either meteorological or internal.
Trace: Yeah, yeah, he's heard all the jokes, trust me. What Trace is, however, is patient, self-confident and quite funny. He was brought up with the capacity to think on his feet and as a very interested person these days, he won't just divvy out his friendship and his time willy nilly.
Tracker: The quiet type. Some people are just better working alone.
Tracy: Tracy is liberal man and a liberal thinker, but he's neither wasteful, slovenly or overtly rude. Yes, occasionally strangers are perplexed when they meet a man and not the woman they anticipated, but this surprise provides Tracy with something of an open window to express what he wants and who he is. Rarely are those strangers let down. Consequently, Tracy was never really destined to think one-dimensionally.
Travis: Travis is harmless enough but he’s a bit silly.
Treeve: The dealer and shaker who looks beyond the surface of things to try and understand what's really going on. Yep, his lady is begging for him to add-on to the back deck, but no way would Treeve do it himself. He can afford a good carpenter, so that's who he'll hire to do it. Fuck it, he might even nick off to Japan for a quick ski holiday while it's being done. No point sitting around here, trying to talk to traders and the crew in the know with all that racket going on outside. Treeve is a happy guy, but he likes his space, and he likes things organised. Don't waste his time by asking him to come over and help fix your fence.
Trehan: Trehan is one of the few men who would perform very well as a mother. No, it's not a gay/feminine reference, more an expression of his capacity to care and watch over those younger people who are either in his charge or around him, in general. Does he have eyes in the back of his head? Almost. Trehan is a careful organiser who likes nice shoes.
Trenam: A suit and tie kind of guy. And that's great, until he finds himself on a tram, train, bus or ferry on the way to work, looking down at himself to discover he's forgotten his trousers and is standing in only a pair of underpants. Trenam, a word of advice: ditch the suit, brother. It was never really you in the first place.
Trent: Tall, blonde and invariably lean from the early years of hard work or hard playing, Trent lives the good life - copywriter, art critic or charter boat skipper - and these days he’s a relaxed character who is enjoying life to the full.
Trenton: In high school he was first in class every time. It was nearly embarrassing.
Trev: Trev is a happy kind of a gumby who manages to hold it all together, usually, and who rarely injures himself, as well as keeping the vehicle in a straight line no matter how much it's raining. The key is to not panic and we may well write this on his gravestone. And no, he's not going anywhere for a while. He's destined to be an old and much loved man. Thanks Trev.
Trevelyan:
No, he's not a bloody trevally, you fool, he's a human, and quite a bizarre one, actually.

Why's that?

Well, look at him. Fuck knows where he bought those green velour trousers from but they're a foot too long, which is a pity because you should see his shoes!

I can't even see his face for hair.

I know. Me neither.

What does he do?

Hah, that's the funny bit. Would you believe me if I told you he's never worked a day in his life?

Yes, I think I would. Did he inherit lots of money?

Mmmm.....I don't know. No one knows. He's got a great stereo though, so perhaps he was a DJ?
Trevor: Ungainly around women and deceptively serious, in general, Trevor never loses sight of his mantra that a fair reward is gained from a fair effort in all aspects of life that matter; food, friendship and construction.
Trey: Trey has learned to confront his fears. It took a while, but it means he now strides through the world doing what he wants without any sense of falseness, guilt or laziness.
Tricky:
Yep, Tricky by name and cheeky by nature, Tricky arrives on the party scene with a reputation and an ego, neither of which you want to miss. And yes, in his younger day, and possibly not even in his younger day, Tricky was a kinky little fucker with a plethora of friends who were more than happy to stoke the fire. None of this shy, quiet and demure bullshit here folks. Tricky is here for this moment we’re standing in, so just strap yourself in (or strap one up), brace yourself for a rockin’ good time and simply jump. At the very least the associated laughter and hubbub which surrounds Tricky will cheer you up. 

The End.
Trimmer: Never heard of the Old Testament, and wouldn’t pay any heed to anyone who did. Trimmer is a fit, busy business man, and he rarely takes his problems home.
Tristan: At the moment of orgasm he yells out, “OH TRISTAN!!! TRISTAN!! GO, TRISTAN, GO!!”
Tristram: Miraculously, Tristram is the only person to yell louder than his close relation, Tristan. Except Tristram yells out, "OH JOYOUS TRISTRAM! HERE ART THOU MOMENT, YOUNG MAN!!"
Trong: Trong plays the bugle and he only knows one way to play: LOUD. He’s tried to play quietly - say, when he's practising late at night - but he's just too passionate about his craft. Go you good thing, Trong!
Troy: Troy breastfed until he was 23 yrs old and this has screwed with his head something chronic.
Tsunami: Really? Tsunami, no offence but your parents are fools. At least they didn’t call you Sandstorm or Tornado, I suppose. Either way, Tsunami can only be a quiet and humble fellow because there is literally no where else for him to go. He has warm eyes and a warm handshake, and he’s no rockstar. What did you want Mum and Dad? For him to end up in fucking jail?
Tub: Round body. Big round smile. Another perpetual young man who rarely does ill in the world. Too nice for politics and not fit enough to spear-fish, he'd make an excellent wine critic.
Tubby: Yeah I know, you wouldn't imagine him to be the world's most adaptive strategist would you? We certianly didn't. And no, the only six-pack he's ever seen is the one he tends to pull out of the fridge, plonk in the esky and take down to the jetty with the rest of his fishing gear.
Tucker: A wanna-be jockey who grew too big by far. You can still him at the racetrack, though. He's the bloke with the syringe, going around and injecting all the horses with the special elixir that makes them run faster.
Tuki: Coke dealer. And no, we're not talking about the drink. How the cops haven't got him yet no one knows. He's always smiling and he never seems to conceal what he does for a living. Perhaps that's why he gets away with it?
Tupou: The name of a completely tame, albeit very rare New Zealand black bear. Yep, he weighs 400kg and he could snap your neck without so much as thinking about it, and he'd probably even quite enjoy eating you if the thought ever occurred to him, but not this guy. He's been surrounded with too much love and attention from when he was a cub. The only thing he would do is snap the neck of anyone or anything trying to harm those he loved, and he's too happy and relaxed to get upset about anything else, so long as he gets his tucker. Tupou.
Twiggy: Twiggy doesn’t seem to be that bright and he doesn’t seem to have that much common sense but he’s a humorous bloke who, once in a while, comes out with these little gems that literally stops everyone in their tracks. It might be an observation or an idea, but they’re worth waiting for. So perhaps he’s not a total dill after all…
Ty: Ty is caught between a rock and a hard place. Society, you see, attempts to brainwash all of us into working hard and pursuing material goals that amount to nothing in the end, really, but people like Ty are almost impossible to get through to, and that's a good thing. For instance, how can you expect a man to dedicate himself to maximising a profit margin when even the meer thought of hooning down a flying fox through a rain forest gets him frothing at the mouth: Ty.
Tye: Tye would love to fly by the seat of his pants and he gets as close as being a good driver when he's sober. If he were a ship he wouldn't leak much.
Tyler:
Option A:  Tyler spent two years in a rehab clinic trying to kick a cocaine habit that cost him his family and most of his friends. These days he can be seen begging for money near the entrance to most train stations, but it was never his fault.

Option B:  Tyler has barely worked a full day in his life, and it must be said that someone shouldn’t, otherwise where are the differences in life? Having said that, it wouldn’t kill him, and as a product of the modern generation he seems to have one eye permanently fixed on the bloody mirror/smartphone screen.
Tynan: Tynan suffers from having well-to-do parents that don't push him. Tynan, I'm sure you know this, but you MUST test yourself, whether you think you're ready for it or not.
Tyree: An usual man. He's no namby-pamby that's for sure. Tyree listens to what people have to say, making a judgement call only then. He's only really dangerous if he gets bored. Is he dyslexic? I only ask that because it seems he's not reading enough.
Tyron: Tryon is an excellent adjudicator.
